title: Why did your AI agent get it wrong? Arize Phoenix shows you
description:
Arize Phoenix is a self-hosted LLM observability and evaluation tool: trace every step of your AI app or agent with OpenTelemetry, grade the answers with LLM-as-a-judge evals, and test prompt changes before you ship.
It's source-available under the Elastic License 2.0: free to self-host, but not to offer to others as a hosted service.

In this video:
- What Arize Phoenix is and how tracing works (each request becomes a tree of steps, with timings and tokens)
- 3 real uses: find the broken step, grade the answers, test a fix before you ship
- The catch: the Elastic License, login off by default, what real self-hosting needs, and how fast it changes
- Who it's for, an alternative, and how to try it

Three real uses:
1. Find the broken step: a trace shows the documents a retriever returned, tool calls, the messages sent to the model, token usage, latency and errors. It works with OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, DSPy, the Vercel AI SDK, the Claude Agent SDK and more, through OpenInference auto-instrumentation.
2. Grade the answers: ready-made LLM-as-a-judge evaluators (hallucination, faithfulness, correctness, retrieval relevance, tool selection and more), code checks (exact match, regex) and human annotations on traces.
3. Test a fix before you ship: replay a traced LLM call in the prompt playground, compare prompt versions side by side, or run an experiment over a saved dataset and compare it with earlier runs.

The catch: the README calls Phoenix open source, but the server is licensed under the Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2), which is source-available, not an OSI-approved open-source licence. You can use, change and self-host it for free, and the docs say there are no feature gates, but you may not provide it to others as a hosted or managed service. (The tracing client, arize-phoenix-otel, is Apache 2.0.) Login is off by default: set PHOENIX_ENABLE_AUTH=True and PHOENIX_SECRET before anyone else can reach it; the first admin login is admin@localhost / admin, and you're asked to change it. SQLite is the default, for local and single-user use; for production the docs recommend PostgreSQL 14+ and a persistent volume, and one instance per team. It moves fast: eight major versions in 2026 (13.0.0 to 20.0.0), so check MIGRATION.md before you upgrade. Basic web analytics are on by default (no trace data, per the README); turn them off with PHOENIX_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false.

Try it (Python 3.11 to 3.14):
pip install arize-phoenix
phoenix serve
Then open http://localhost:6006. Or run uvx arize-phoenix serve, or the Docker image: docker run -p 6006:6006 -p 4317:4317 -i -t arizephoenix/phoenix:latest
To send traces from your app, follow the tracing quickstart (pip install arize-phoenix-otel plus the instrumentor for your provider). You need your own model API key.
